No medical expenses (Schedule A line 1 $0). Line 2 enters line 11b at no less than zero (amb.2025.sa_medical_negative_agi), so line 3 is $0, line 4 is $0 and line 17 is $0; the signed reading would give line 3 -$450 and line 4 $450.

Predicted by hand from the archived text before recording (BUG-0094): the same return as audit.sa.negative_agi_medical with $1,000 of medical and dental expenses on Schedule A line 1; adjusted gross income -$6,000. Line 2 $0, line 3 $0, line 4 $1,000 - $0 = $1,000 (the whole of line 1, never more), line 17 $1,000 (no other itemized deductions); the signed reading would give line 4 $1,450.

Stage 13, predicted by hand from the archived instructions before recording: married filing separately (refused overall at Schedule 3 line 11; Schedule A still figured): state and local income tax $30,000; AGI $100,000 below the $250,000 threshold for a separate return, so the $40,000 ceiling is not reduced; half for a separate return, $20,000; line 5e the smaller of $30,000 and $20,000, $20,000.

Stage 13, predicted by hand from the archived instructions before recording: as above with AGI $400,000: $150,000 over the $250,000 threshold, reduced by 30% = $45,000, the ceiling $40,000 - $45,000 is below the $10,000 floor, so $10,000; half, $5,000; line 5e $5,000.

Stage 16, predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi (Schedule 1 line 8, Schedule A, the Tax Table, the EIC), i1040sca, i1040s8812 and p525, by two independent agents that did not see the encoding and agreed on every shared value; recorded after comparison. Facts: Single. Wages $60,000. Gambling winnings $5,000 (Form W-2G box 1); gambling losses $7,000. State income tax paid $4,000; home mortgage interest (Form 1098) $9,000. Working (predictor A): s1 8b gambling winnings 5,000 (i1040gi Line 8b p.90); s1 9 = 5,000; s1 10 = 5,000 -> f1040 line 8. f1040 1z 60,000; 9 = 65,000; 10 = 0; 11a/11b AGI 65,000. Sch A: 5a 4,000; 5d 4,000; 5e smaller of 5d or 40,000 = 4,000 (AGI under 500,000; f1040sa line 5e); 7 = 4,000; 8a 9,000; 8e 9,000; 10 9,000; 16 gambling losses only to the extent of winnings on s1 8b (i1040sca line 16): min(7,000, 5,000) = 5,000; 17 = 4,000+9,000+5,000 = 18,000 > standard 15,750 (single, i1040gi Standard Deduction) so itemize: 12e = 18,000; 14 = 18,000; 15 = 65,000 - 18,000 = 47,000; 16 Tax Table single 47,000-47,050 = 5,405; 18 = 5,405 (no Schedule 2).

BUG-0084. Joint return, wages $60,000 and $50,000; the spouse was born in 1960, has no SSN valid for employment and died in 2025 before reaching 65. i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, Death of spouse in 2025, "don't check the box that says 'Spouse was born before January 2, 1961'"; p501 p. 23: no age box, so the MFJ base $31,500 (line 12e), line 15 $78,500 and Tax Table tax $8,946 (line 16, the $78,500 to $78,550 row, married filing jointly).

Simultaneous refusals (precedence), with every answer of stage16.refund.f7 given: Yes to the Schedule A charitable limitation screen and Yes to Form 8938. Adjusted gross income, and so Schedule A line 4, refuses for Form 8938; Schedule A line 17 checks its own entries before its operands, so it refuses for the charitable limitation. The refused value is the evaluator's.

cases.evidence_note: Mutation fixture (lane mint), expected values predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. Inputs of classm.tipjob.1 (single filer, home owner) with $12,000 of mortgage interest reported on Form 1098, no mortgage interest or points paid outside a Form 1098, no other use of the proceeds, and the answer that the interest is limited by the debt or fair-market-value limits. i1040sca p. 8, Limits on home mortgage interest: "deduct home mortgage interest on up to $750,000 ($375,000 if you are married filing separately) of that debt ... See Pub. 936 to figure your deduction", and Line 8a, "Home mortgage interest limited. If your home mortgage interest deduction is limited, see Pub. 936 to figure the amount". On a return that is not married filing separately with interest on line 8a the joint-limits question applies, so its gate is true, and the limited interest is a Schedule A item this tool does not compute (sa.unsupported true).

Lane bugfix-other, predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. BUG-0972. mfs.sa.spouse_itemizes_return (married filing separately, the spouse itemizes, state income tax withheld $3,000) with a Yes to the question whether the itemized costs were paid from an account held with the husband or wife or the two file a joint state return. i1040sca p. 1, "If you and your spouse paid expenses jointly and are filing separate returns for 2025, see Pub. 504"; p504 p. 5, Table 1 divides such expenses (half of jointly paid medical costs; a gross-income fraction of state tax on a joint state return), which this tool does not apply. The return is married filing separately and itemizes (the spouse itemizes, so the standard deduction is zero), so the question is asked and line 12e (sa.deduction) refuses at sa.mfs_joint_paid_if_itemizing.

sa.deduction.form: Schedule A on a separate return, expenses paid jointly with the spouse (Pub. 504, Table 1)
sa.deduction.remedy: On a married filing separately return, itemized deductions paid from money held with your spouse, or state income tax on a joint state return, are divided between you under Pub. 504; that is outside this tool.

cases.evidence_note: Health insurance above the Form 7206 limit (i7206 p. 2, "any medical insurance payments not deductible on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 17, can be included as medical expenses on Schedule A"). Wages $30,000; Schedule C line 1 $5,000; premiums $8,000 under the business. Form 7206 line 14 is $4,646.76 (the profit less the deductible part of SE tax, $353.24), so $3,353.24 is not deducted. AGI is $30,000 + $5,000 - $353.24 - $4,646.76 = $30,000.00; line 3 is $2,250.00. Other medical costs $1,000, so line 1 is $4,353.24 and line 4 $2,103.24 by hand.

Predicted by hand before recording from p527 p. 25 and p936 p. 4: single, wages $50,000; a vacation home rented 200 fair days and used 10 personal days (not a home), Form 1098 interest $12,000 and property tax $3,000, all entered with the rental; the filer leaves the rental out of Schedule A as the help says. Schedule E line 16 = $3,000 x 200/210 = $2,857.14; the $142.86 left is added to Schedule A line 5b; none of the interest is on line 8a (not a qualified home). Line 17 = $2,500 state tax + $142.86 + $9,000 gifts = $11,642.86, so the standard deduction applies.
